cards.explanation: The answer is False. The bush is ablaze, and the text says it “…was not consumed.” (Exodus 3:2) Moses, Israel's leader, is staring at a fire that doesn't finish its job. If my ovens did that, friends, I'd call it a very patient batch.

Moses goes over to look. He thinks, “I must go over and see this marvelous sight. Why is the bush not burning up?” (Exodus 3:3) Honestly, I'd have gone over too, friends. I'd have walked over so fast my gold base would have left skid marks.
The answer is “Here I am…” (Exodus 3:4) Short, plain and ready. Not a bad way to answer when your name gets called from a bush, friends.

The answer is holy. God says, “Do not come any closer… Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.” (Exodus 3:5) Moses is out in the wilderness at the mountain of God, and God is calling to him from the bush. The ground gets called holy, and God tells him to take his sandals off.

The answer is True. After God says He is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses hides his face. (Exodus 3:6) The text says he “…was afraid to look at God.” I think anyone would do the same, friends.

The answer is that God has come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. He says, “I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians…” (Exodus 3:8) He has seen and heard, and He has come down to act. That's a God who shows up.

The answer is Pharaoh. God says, “I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.” (Exodus 3:10) Pharaoh is the king of Egypt. A few verses ago Moses was minding Jethro's flock, and now he's got a king on his schedule.

The answer is “I will surely be with you…” (Exodus 3:12) Notice that Moses asks who he is, and God answers with who is going with him. That answer is better than anything Moses could have said about himself, friends.

The answer is mountain. God says, “When you have brought the people out of Egypt, all of you will worship God on this mountain.” (Exodus 3:12) Moses is standing at that mountain right now. The sign comes after the job is done.
The answer is “I AM WHO I AM.” (Exodus 3:14) Then God tells Moses what to say to the Israelites: “‘I AM has sent me to you.’…” Moses asked for a name, and this is the name God gave him.

The answer is False. God says, “This is My name forever, and this is how I am to be remembered in every generation.” (Exodus 3:15) Forever, friends, not just for Moses' day. Every generation is a long line of people, and God says that's how long the name stands.

The answer is True. God tells Moses, “The elders of Israel will listen to what you say…” (Exodus 3:18) Moses hasn't said a word to them yet, and God is already telling him how that part goes. I'd love that before a big meeting at work, friends: the room is already listening.

The answer is that the king won't let them go without a mighty hand. God says, “But I know that the king of Egypt will not allow you to go unless a mighty hand compels him.” (Exodus 3:19) So Moses gets the hard news up front. And God follows it with His plan to stretch out His hand.
The answer is release. God says, “And after that, he will release you.” (Exodus 3:20) First come the wonders, and after that, the king lets them go.

The answer is silver and gold jewelry and clothing. God says every woman will ask “…her neighbor and any woman staying in her house for silver and gold jewelry and clothing…” (Exodus 3:22) Just before that, He says, “…you will not go away empty-handed.” (Exodus 3:21) I like that God gets specific, friends. He doesn't just say it'll be fine, He names the jewelry and the clothing.
The answer is staff. The LORD asks, “What is that in your hand?” and Moses answers, “A staff,” (Exodus 4:2) Just a plain shepherd's stick. Hold on to that thought, friends.

The answer is that he runs from it. The text says Moses threw it on the ground, “…and it became a snake, and he ran from it.” (Exodus 4:3) Honestly, friends, I'd be gone before my own mustache caught up.

The answer is True. Moses reaches out and grabs the snake, “…and it turned back into a staff in his hand.” (Exodus 4:4) The LORD had told him to grab it by the tail. I think that took some nerve after running from it.

The answer is leprous and white as snow. Moses took his hand out of his cloak, “…and when he took it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.” (Exodus 4:6) The LORD had just told him to put it inside. It's the second sign the LORD gives him.
The answer is False. The text says, “…it was restored, like the rest of his skin.” (Exodus 4:7) The LORD has Moses put the hand back inside the cloak first. Then it comes out whole again.
The answer is blood. The LORD says, “Then the water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground.” (Exodus 4:9) That's the third sign, for if they don't believe the first two.

The point is that the LORD gave man his mouth. He asks, “Who gave man his mouth? Or who makes the mute or the deaf, the sighted or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?” (Exodus 4:11) Moses talks about his mouth, and the LORD reminds him Who made it.

The answer is that the LORD promises to help him speak and teach him what to say. He says, “Now go! I will help you as you speak, and I will teach you what to say.” (Exodus 4:12) Moses doesn't have to come up with the words alone, friends. The LORD promises help and teaching.

The answer is “Please send someone else.” Moses says, “Please, Lord, send someone else.” (Exodus 4:13) That comes right after the signs and the LORD's promise to help. I can't judge him, friends, because I once asked an angel if he had the right drawer.

The answer is Aaron. The LORD says, “Is not Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he can speak well, and he is now on his way to meet you.” (Exodus 4:14) Moses is also told Aaron is coming to him. The LORD already has the helper on the road.

The answer is True. The LORD says of Aaron, “When he sees you, he will be glad in his heart.” (Exodus 4:14) The LORD also says Aaron is now on his way to meet Moses. Moses had just asked for someone else to go, and the LORD answers with a brother who will be glad to see him.
